Privacy Policy

Last updated: 17 October 2026 [TO CONFIRM: effective date]

Who we are

Yestermanac is an “On This Day” almanac app. It is published by MidMightBit Games (Australia) [TO CONFIRM: legal entity name and ABN] (“we”, “us”). We are responsible for the data described here.

Privacy contact: aardappvark@proton.me [TO CONFIRM: privacy contact address].

The short version

  • There is no account. You do not give us your name or email address to use the app.
  • There are no adverts, no advertising identifiers and no third-party tracking or analytics libraries in the app.
  • Most of what you do in the app is stored only on your device.
  • Some features need the network. Each one, and exactly what it sends, is listed on the Data & Location page.
  • The app never asks for precise (GPS-level) location. It asks for approximate location only when you tap “Use my location”.

What is stored on your device

The app keeps the following in its private storage on your device:

  • Your settings: content language, countries and region, mixes, filters, year style, notification times, widget style, theme and the usage-counts switch.
  • Your home state or province for holiday reminders, if you choose one.
  • Your almanac place: a city you picked or, if you used “Use my location”, coordinates rounded to 0.1° (about 11 km) and a place name.
  • Your birthday (day and month) for “your birthday in history”, if you enter it.
  • Your full date of birth, and the people and dates you save, in “The day you were born”.
  • If you switch on Birthdays (Pro): the names and birthdays read from your contacts and calendars, a key that lets the app find the contact again, and your message preferences, including the name you sign with. Phone numbers are not stored.
  • Favourites, notes and your own dates.
  • Quiz, game and reading progress.
  • If you connect a wallet: your public wallet address, the wallet's name, the signed sign-in message and your Seeker Genesis Token status. The address and sign-in message are saved only in encrypted storage; if the device cannot provide it, the address is kept in memory only.
  • Your Pro status and the signature of your payment transaction.
  • Correction reports waiting to be sent.
  • A random install identifier, created on first use. The app sends it to the Yestermanac service to obtain a short-lived session, so that the service can apply each installation's daily limit. It is not linked to your name or device. It is linked to a wallet only if you buy or restore Pro: the app then asks your wallet to sign a message naming this install identifier, and sends that signature, your public wallet address and the payment's transaction signature to the Yestermanac service, which checks the payment on the blockchain and records the wallet address with this installation so that Pro applies to it.

Clearing the app's data in Android settings, or uninstalling the app, removes all of this from the device.

Contacts and calendars (optional)

Only if you switch on a source in Settings → Birthdays, the app asks for permission to read your contacts or your calendars. Google (Gmail) and Outlook accounts that sync to your phone are read through these same Android stores; the app never signs in to Google or Microsoft. It reads only birthdays: from contacts, the name and the birthday; from calendars you choose, yearly events that are birthdays. When you send a message to someone from your contacts, the app looks up that contact's phone number at that moment and hands it, with the message, to your messaging app; the number is not stored. None of this is sent to us or to anyone else. Switching a source off removes what it imported; you can revoke either permission in Android settings at any time. If you switch on name days, it also reads your contacts’ names, and the country code of their phone numbers to choose each person’s name-day calendar (name days differ by country), to match them to the calendar; they are read on the phone each time and not stored. Only the calendar you choose for a person is kept, on this device. With Pro, “Write with AI” sends only the occasion, language, theme, relation and age to our service, which asks Claude (Anthropic, as our processor) to write the message; the name is added on your phone and nothing is kept.

Android backup

Android can back up app data to your Google account if backup is switched on for your device. This happens under Google's terms, not ours, and we cannot read those backups.

  • Never included in backup or device transfer: wallet data, your date of birth, saved people and imported birthdays, the install identifier, your Pro status and payment signature, your settings (including your region, almanac place and birthday), favourites and notes, your own dates, and correction reports waiting to be sent. Pro moves to a new device only through “Restore purchase”, which checks your payment on the blockchain.
  • May be included: the rest, such as quiz, game and reading progress and the list of reminders already shown.

You can switch Android backup off in your device settings.

What leaves your device

The app sends data only for the features below. The Data & Location page gives the details for each one.

  • Solana network (Seeker Genesis Token check, Pro payment, restore purchase): your public wallet address and your IP address reach a Solana RPC provider.
  • Pictures: when an entry has a picture, it is loaded from Wikimedia servers, which receive your IP address.
  • Anonymous usage counts: event names only, such as “app_open”. On by default; you can switch them off in Settings.
  • Yestermanac service: correction reports you write, and lookups in “The day you were born”, which include the date you look up, your time zone and your home country and region. Requests to the service also carry a short-lived session obtained with the random install identifier. For languages without a bundled pack, the service also receives the date and language of each day the app loads, and your search words when you search; if you link Pro, it receives your public wallet address, the wallet's signature and the payment's transaction signature.
  • Approximate location, only when you tap “Use my location”: Android's place-name lookup (the Geocoder) turns it into a state, province, country or place name. Depending on your device, it may use Google's network service to do so. It is never read when the app starts or before a payment.
  • Links you open (sources, maps, further reading) are handed to your browser or maps app.

Anonymous usage counts

To see which features are used, the app can send the name of an event, such as “app_open”, “settings_opened” or “payments_sol”. The request contains the event name and the app's own service key. It contains no user ID, device ID, install ID, wallet address, date or text you entered.

Like any internet request, it reaches our server from your IP address, and the server works out your country from it. [TO CONFIRM: whether the analytics server or its host keeps IP addresses in logs, and for how long].

Nothing is counted or sent before you accept the welcome screen. After that, counting is on by default, and you can switch it off at any time in Settings → Privacy.

In the current build the counting service is not connected, so nothing is sent. [TO CONFIRM: status at release].

Why we use data

  • To provide the features you ask for, including Pro, payment and restore (performance of a contract).
  • To check regional availability required by sanctions law (legal obligation and legitimate interests).
  • To count anonymous usage and keep the service secure (legitimate interests). You can object by switching counting off.
  • Approximate location, only with your permission (consent). You can withdraw it in Android settings.

[TO CONFIRM: legal bases for each market, reviewed by counsel].

Who receives data

We do not sell personal data and we do not share it for advertising. Data reaches these parties only as described above:

  • Solana RPC providers: api.mainnet-beta.solana.com and solana-rpc.publicnode.com. [TO CONFIRM: whether the release build also carries a Helius fallback endpoint].
  • The Wikimedia Foundation, which serves pictures.
  • Anthropic, which runs the Claude model that writes Pro “Write with AI” messages, receiving only the occasion, language, theme, relation and age.
  • The provider that hosts our services. [TO CONFIRM: hosting provider (planned: Cloudflare) and its data processing terms].
  • Google or your device maker, through Android's Geocoder and backup, under their own terms.

Payments are made on the public Solana blockchain. Your wallet address, the amount and the time are public and permanent. Neither we nor anyone else can delete them.

How long data is kept

  • On your device: until you delete it, clear the app's data or uninstall the app.
  • Correction reports on our service: the entry ID, language, your note and the time. Reports from the app carry no identifier for you. [TO CONFIRM: retention period].
  • Lookups in “The day you were born”: [TO CONFIRM: whether the service logs request details, and for how long].
  • Usage counts: [TO CONFIRM: retention period for counts and for any server logs].

International transfers

Our services and the providers above may process data outside your country, including in Australia and the United States. [TO CONFIRM: transfer safeguards, for example standard contractual clauses].

Your rights

Depending on where you live (for example under the Australian Privacy Act 1988, the EU or UK GDPR, or Californian law), you can ask to access, correct or delete personal data we hold, object to its use, or withdraw consent. Write to the contact address above. Because there is no account and our servers keep almost no data, there is often nothing linked to you that we can find.

You can also complain to your data protection authority. In Australia this is the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC). [TO CONFIRM: EU and UK representative, if required].

Children

The app is for people aged 18 and over [TO CONFIRM: minimum age]. It is not directed at children.

Security

Wallet data is kept in encrypted storage and is excluded from backups. Connections to our services use HTTPS. We never see or hold your wallet's private keys.

Changes

When this policy changes we will update this page and its date. Significant changes will also be shown in the app.
